The Labour Department announced today (10th) that Wa So Cafe (Prince Edward) provided false information to the department during its local open recruitment period when applying to import foreign workers. The department imposed administrative sanctions, including immediately terminating the company's application and refusing to process any applications submitted by the company in the following year. Related report: Importing Foreign Workers | Why were 18 cases given administrative sanctions? 1365 complaints received over three years, about 10% received warnings or administrative sanctions

Wa So Cafe (Prince Edward) was administratively sanctioned by the Labour Department for providing false information during its local open recruitment period.

A spokesperson for the Labour Department said that after investigation, it was confirmed that Wa So Cafe (Prince Edward) provided false information during its local open recruitment period when applying to import waiters/waitresses, junior chefs and dishwashers, violating the requirements of the "Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme". Administrative sanctions were therefore imposed. The department has immediately terminated the company's submitted application for importing foreign workers, and refused to process any applications submitted by the company under the Enhanced Scheme in the following year.

The department emphasised that employers importing foreign workers must strictly comply with the scheme's requirements, including giving priority to hiring suitable local workers. If employers violate labour or immigration laws, the Enhanced Scheme or standard employment contract requirements, the Labour Department will impose administrative sanctions, including terminating applications already submitted by employers, revoking import worker approvals already obtained by employers, and refusing to process applications subsequently submitted by employers.

Including Wa So Cafe (Prince Edward) whose sanction was just announced today, FactWire compiled information on 18 companies penalised for violating import foreign worker regulations. Among them, 10 companies are in the catering services and cleaning industries. Why were they penalised? Among the 18 companies, 9 were involved in unreasonably refusing to hire local job seekers, and most had their subsequent two-year import foreign worker applications rejected by the Labour Department. Another two restaurants dismissed local employees after importing foreign workers, and their already-granted foreign worker approvals were immediately revoked.
